_comment: CLAUDE.md size ratchet CEILING (W1-T503, MASTER-PLAN §8A). Captured via `node scripts/claude-md-budget-ratchet.mjs` against the committed CLAUDE.md. capBytes is now a ROUND BOUNDARY (65536 = 64 KiB) carrying deliberate headroom over the measured figure, which is a change from the zero-headroom shape this baseline held until 2026-08-22 -- see bumpRationale for why the operator made it and what it is NOT. The ceiling still fails closed and still only ever ratchets UP by a reviewed bump that says why growth is right; never lower it to make a red PR pass, and never raise it to paper over an unreviewed dump of new rules.
bumpRationale: Raised 62733 -> 65536 (64 KiB) by an OPERATOR DECISION on 2026-08-22, and the reason is the cost of the old shape rather than the size of the file. THE ZERO-HEADROOM CEILING WAS RETIRED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Holding capBytes == measuredBytes made every edit pay a fold tax whether or not it had anything left to fold: the file hit the cap with ONE BYTE of room twice on the SAME DAY, and both times the lane spent more effort compressing prose than writing the rule it came to write -- the first paid 283 bytes across nine citation folds, the second paid eleven lines across three more. The cheap folds are spent, so the next fold would have cost meaning rather than duplication. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the ratchet still fails closed, still runs unconditionally in ci.yml, and still reports size against cap on every run. The intent is that an edit DELIBERATES about its own cost, not that every edit pays a tax at the moment it happens. 65536 is chosen as a round, legible boundary rather than an arbitrary figure -- +2803 bytes over the retired cap, roughly six to eight rules at the observed size of that day's additions. AND THIS IS THE SECOND CONVERSATION ABOUT THIS NUMBER, NOT THE FIRST: a later reader proposing another raise should know the operator has already granted one, and should say what changed since -- 'the folds are expensive now' was the argument that carried this time and cannot carry twice without new evidence.
